name: WikiText
description: A language modeling dataset constructed using text extracted from Wikipedia articles that fit the Good or Featured article criteria. The dataset is available in two sizes: WikiText-2 (2 million tokens) and WikiText-103 (103 million tokens). Both feature punctuation, original casing, larger vocabularies, and numbers, making them more realistic for language modeling than the Penn Treebank.
creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher
citeAs: Merity, S., Xiong, C., Bradbury, J., & Socher, R. (2016). Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models. arXiv preprint arXiv:1609.07843.
rai:dataCollection: Text extracted from Wikipedia articles using the Wikipedia API. Articles were selected based on fitting the Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors on Wikipedia. These articles have been reviewed by humans and are considered well written, factually accurate, broad in coverage, neutral in point of view, and stable. This resulted in 23,805 Good articles and 4,790 Featured articles.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Wikipedia articles extracted using the Wikipedia API. Selected articles fitting Good or Featured article criteria (23,805 Good articles and 4,790 Featured articles).
rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Specific sections which primarily featured lists were removed by default. Other minor bugs, such as sort keys and Edit buttons that leaked in from the HTML, were also removed. Mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with <formula> tokens.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Extracting raw text from Wikipedia mark-up using the Wikipedia API. Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer, slightly augmented to further split numbers (8,600 → 8 @,@ 600) and with some additional minor fixes. A vocabulary was constructed by discarding all words with a count below 3. Words outside of the vocabulary were mapped to the <unk> token.
rai:dataUseCases: Language modeling, training and evaluation of neural sequence models. The dataset allows for learning and evaluation of longer term dependencies compared to Penn Treebank. Suitable for testing models on rare words and realistic vocabularies.
